rows.answer: Yes, in part. Section 2 appoints the Agent as the Company's and the Bank's exclusive financial advisor and marketing agent for the Offering, covering best-efforts solicitation of subscriptions and advice on the sale of the Shares. Section 19 states the agreement is the exclusive agreement among the parties on its subject matter, superseding prior agreements.
The agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to principles of conflicts of law.

The excerpts do not state that either party may terminate without cause by giving notice. They describe the Agent's termination right for specified events such as market disruption or material adverse change, and the Company's or Bank's right to terminate if the Agent is in material breach and does not cure it after notice, but they do not address a general termination right without cause.

The excerpts do not address intellectual property created by either party or whether such property becomes owned by the other party. They cover the Bank's organization and licensing, title to real property and other assets, and the ownership of the Bank's capital stock and subsidiaries.

Yes, but only one direction is addressed: Bioamber has the right to audit Cargill's time sheets, once per year during reasonable business hours by an independent third party agreed to by both parties. The excerpts do not provide any right for Cargill to audit Bioamber's records.

The excerpts do not address automatic renewal. Section 10.1 states the agreement runs for four years and may be extended only by mutual written agreement, but the excerpts do not say whether it renews automatically.

Section 10.2 allows termination by written notice only in cases of the other party's bankruptcy or insolvency, or a material default, and also upon mutual written agreement. The excerpts do not address any broader right to terminate for convenience.

Yes. The general waiver of special, incidental, consequential and punitive damages does not apply to liability for breach of confidentiality obligations under Article 10, and it does not limit the parties' indemnification obligations under Article 12. The excerpts do not state that liability for these items is literally unlimited in amount, only that the damages waiver does not cover them.

Yes, the contract limits liability for certain damages: neither party can recover special, incidental, consequential, or punitive damages from the other in connection with the agreement or any license granted under it. This limitation does not apply to liability for breach of confidentiality obligations under Article 10, nor does it limit the parties' indemnification obligations under Article 12.

The excerpts do not state a notice period for stopping the agreement from renewing. Section 11.1 allows renewal only by mutual written agreement for one-year periods, but no non-renewal notice period is given. The excerpts do cover termination for convenience on 120 days' written notice under Section 11.2(b), which is a different mechanism from non-renewal.

Either Party can stop the Contract from automatically renewing by serving written notice of termination at least 65 days before the end of the Initial Term or any subsequent extension. Notice served with less than that period is invalid and of no effect.
No. Section 12.1 provides that neither Party may assign any of its rights or duties under the contract to third parties without the written consent of the other Party.

The excerpts do not state a cap or limit on either party's liability for damages. Yes, but only for the Sponsor: it is not liable for errors of judgment, mistakes of law, or acts or omissions in its duties, except for willful misfeasance, bad faith, gross negligence, or reckless disregard of its obligations. The excerpts do not state any limitation on the Trust's liability.

The excerpts show that MMI is not liable for indirect or consequential damages unless caused by intention or gross negligence, which implies liability for such damages is excluded except in those cases. MMI's indemnity obligations for activities under the Agreement and for third-party patent or copyright infringement claims are stated without an express monetary limit.

Yes. The liability cap does not apply to breaches of Section 8 (confidentiality), so for such breaches the cap and the exclusion of consequential damages do not apply. The cap also excludes claims for monies due. The excerpts do not expressly say liability is wholly unlimited for those claims, only that the £200,000 cap does not apply to them.

Yes. Section 4.5 provides that each Party must retain its financial records relating to payments owed or paid under the Agreement for six years, but the excerpts do not describe any right for one party to inspect the other's books or records; the clause only imposes a retention obligation.

The excerpts do not provide a general right to terminate without cause by simply giving notice. No. Section 34.3 states that HealthGate shall not transfer or assign the whole or any part of the Agreement without the prior written consent of the Publishers. The excerpts provided do not contain an equivalent restriction on the Publishers' right to assign.

Yes, one category is excluded from the liability cap: personal injury or death caused by either party's negligence, for which by law no limit applies. Outside that exception, each party's liability for performance or non-performance is capped at an aggregate amount equal to payments made under the Agreement.

Yes, under Section 5.3 either Party may terminate the Agreement for any reason upon thirty (30) days' written notice to the other Party, unless that Party is itself a Defaulting Party under the Agreement.
No. Under Section 7.5, a party may not assign the agreement without the prior written consent of the other party.

The excerpts do not contain any limitation of liability clause, so they do not state whether liability is capped or unlimited. Section 5.2 allows the non-Defaulting Party to recover damages from the Defaulting Party, but the excerpts do not say whether those damages are limited in amount.

Yes. At the end of the initial three-year term, and at the end of any renewed term, the agreement automatically renews for an additional one-year term, unless a party gives written notice at least six months before the end of the term. During a renewed term, any party may also terminate on six months' prior notice.

To stop the agreement from automatically renewing, a Party must give written notice of its intent to terminate at least six (6) months before the end of the Initial Term or the then current Extension Period.

The excerpts do not show a general right to terminate without cause. Either Party may end the Agreement at the close of the Initial Term or an Extension Period by giving written notice at least six months in advance, and the Agreement otherwise continues automatically. Termination for a prolonged Force Majeure event requires a Termination Notice given at least twelve months before the end of the Force Majeure Period.

The excerpts do not contain any provision establishing exclusive dealing obligations or rights, such as a requirement that a party deal only with the other party for the relevant services. The excerpts do not contain any provision addressing ownership of intellectual property created by either party, so the contract does not appear to cover whether such IP would transfer to the other party.

Yes, in part. The excerpts do not address ownership of other intellectual property created by a party, beyond the Brand and its associated goodwill.

No. Licensee may not assign, transfer, pledge, mortgage or otherwise encumber the agreement without Licensor's prior written consent, which Licensor may give or withhold in its sole discretion, with only a narrow exception for an assignment outside bankruptcy to a successor organization resulting solely from a name change. Even a merger, change of control, reorganization or sale of substantially all of Licensee's stock is treated as an assignment requiring consent, and an attempted assignment in violation is void and results in immediate termination.

The excerpts do not contain a non-compete or any restriction on either party competing with the other. The agreement does not renew in the usual sense because it has no fixed term to renew; it commences on the Effective Date and continues in perpetuity unless terminated under Sections 4.2 through 4.4.

They cover a right of first refusal on any bona fide offer to sell, transfer or convey stock in or assets of Licensor, and an option for Licensee to purchase Licensor's assets or stock, but they do not specifically describe what happens upon a change of control.

Either party can stop the agreement from renewing by delivering written notice of termination to the other party at least sixty (60) days before the end of the original term or any renewal term. The original term runs through March 31, 2004, and renewals are for one-year periods.

The excerpts provided do not address ownership of intellectual property created by either party, so they do not answer whether such IP would transfer to the other party. The excerpts only cover royalty advance and payment terms (Section 3.2) and some general amendment boilerplate and signature blocks.

The excerpts provided do not address whether either party has the right to audit the other's books or records. They cover the change to an exclusive distributorship, a right of first refusal, and an option to purchase, but nothing on audit rights.

No. Neither party may assign or otherwise transfer the agreement to any person or entity without the other's written consent, which may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, and any assignment in violation of this is null and void.

Yes. Section 11 bars either party from liability for indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, and caps E.piphany's liability at the total payments HSNS made under the initial term of the agreement. Section 12.4 also bars either party from liability for lost prospective profits or anticipated sales arising from a termination.

The excerpts do not establish whether the agreement creates exclusive dealing obligations or rights in general. The excerpts do not contain a non-compete or any restriction on either party competing with the other. They only cover taxes, audit rights, ownership of deliverables, trademark challenges, and confidentiality, so this question cannot be answered from the provided text.

No. Section 18 provides that no party may transfer or assign its rights or obligations under the Agreement without the prior written consent of the other parties, and any non-compliant transfer is void.

Yes, in part. The Agents are appointed as the exclusive agents of the Corporation to offer the Offered Shares, though the Agents are under no obligation to purchase any shares. Those are carve-outs from indemnity rather than a general liability limit, and the excerpts do not address the Agents' liability to the Corporation beyond the termination provision.
